newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Forrestania finds new nickel ore body.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Forrestania finds new nickel ore body.

text.p: Metals miner Forrestania Gold NL said on Friday it had found a significant new nickel mineralised zone on the Roundtop Joint Venture three kilometres north of its Maggie Hays deposit in Western Australia.

The Roundtop Joint Venture is itself a joint venture between Capricorn Resources NL with 25 percent and the Lake Johnston Joint Vetnure with 75 percent. Lake Johnston is equally owned by Forrestania and South Africa's Gencor Ltd.
Forrestania said one drill hole had intersected 10.7 metres at 2.39 percent nickel from 164 metres with a broader zone of 14.7 metres at 1.94 percent.
"An additional 0.85 metre zone of massive sulphides returned an intersection of 8.98 percent nickel from 187.45 metres," it said.
Forrestania Managing Director Barry Eldridge said the mineralisation found was of a similar style to the Maggie Hays deposit.
Eldridge also said drilling 300 metres to 400 metres south of Maggie Hays had encountered two intersections of about 20 metres in width containing disseminated nickel sulphide mineralisation.
"Assays from these two diamond drill holes have not yet been received, but they have the potential to significantly increase the strike length of the Maggie Hays orebody," he said.

Forrestania and Gencor are spending about A$8.7 million during the current financial year with the intention of commmencing a bankable feasibility study in the September 1997 quarter on the Lake Johnston joint venture.
Forrestania is currently under a friendly cash and scrip takeover offer by Vancouver-based Lionore Mining International Ltd.

The most recent resource figure for Maggie Hays shows a total of 11.9 million tonnes of material, grading an average 1.55 grams per tonne of nickel and 0.05 percent cobalt, equivalent to 184,880 tonnes of nickel and 5,523 tonnes of cobalt.
Construction is expected take about 18 months, with production starting around mid-1999.
Eldridge has estimated the total capital cost of the Maggie Hays project would be about A$250 million.
He has said the project would operate at an average cost of about US$1.50 per pound of nickel.
Forrestania Gold's shares were two cents lower at A$2.85 at 3.40 p.m. (0440 GMT).
